title: Food and cooking
cando: buy food, and follow and give a simple recipe

about.text: In this lesson you buy food at a stall, and you cook. You ask for amounts: a kilo of rice, a tin of tomatoes. Then you read a recipe. You also explain how to make a dish you know.
goals: Buy food with amounts: a kilo of rice, a packet of butter, two tins of tomatoes.
Say an apple, but some rice.
Follow a recipe and read a food label.
Give instructions in order: first, then, after that, finally.
Explain how to make a dish, then buy what you need.

chapters.title: At the stall
chapters.text:
In this lesson you buy food, and you cook.
First, Kwame buys food at a stall in the market.
Listen for the amounts: a kilo of rice, a packet of butter, two tins of tomatoes.
The stallholder asks: Anything else?
Kwame says what he wants: I'll have a piece, please.
When you have everything, say: That's all, thanks.

chapters.title: Some rice, a packet of rice
chapters.text:
Now two grammar points.
One: you can count apples and eggs. An apple, two eggs.
You can't count rice, butter or cheese. Say some rice, some butter.
To count them, say a packet of rice, a piece of cheese, two tins of soup.
Two: instructions. An instruction starts with the verb. Cut the onions. Add the rice.
Put the steps in order with first, then, after that and finally.

chapters.title: A recipe and a label
chapters.text:
Next, you read the back of a packet of rice.
The label tells you how to cook the rice and where to keep it.
The recipe has two parts: what you need, and what to do.
Read what you need first. Then follow the steps in order.
After that, you write a recipe for a dish you know.

chapters.title: Explain a dish
chapters.text:
Then you explain how to make a dish from your home.
Say the steps in order: first, then, after that, finally.
Then you go to a stall and buy what you need, with the amounts.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about food and cooking.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: Who usually cooks in your home?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people cook every day. Some people buy lunch at work and only cook at the weekend.

conversation.title: At the food stall
conversation.setting: Kwame is cooking dinner for friends on Saturday. He is at a food stall at the market.
lines: Hello! What can I get you?
Hi. Can I have a kilo of rice, please?
Yes. Two tins of tomatoes and a bottle of oil.
A big bottle or a small one?
A small one, please. Have you got any chicken?
Sorry, we don't sell meat. Try the stall at the end.
Yes, it's from a farm near here. Keep it in the fridge.
I'll have a piece, please. About 250 grams.
A packet of butter and a jar of coffee. That's all, thanks.

sound.title: ch or sh: cheese and fresh
sound.explain: Cheese and chicken start with ch, like cheap. Fresh and fish have sh, like shop. For ch, stop the air, then let it go. For sh, the air does not stop. Listen, then say each group.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Three ask for food. The last one tells Kwame what to do.
examples: Can I have a kilo of rice, please?
Two tins of tomatoes and a bottle of oil.
spot.question: Which words help you count rice and cheese? What is the first word in Keep it in the fridge?
spot.answer: You can't count rice or cheese. So you say a kilo of rice and a piece of cheese. You can count tins and bottles: two tins, a bottle. Keep it in the fridge is an instruction. It starts with the verb, with no I or you.

rules.title: An apple, some rice, a packet of rice
rule: You can count it: an apple, two apples, an egg, six eggs.
You can't count it: some rice, some milk, some cheese. Not: a rice, two rices.
To count it, say how it comes: a packet of rice, a tin of soup, a kilo of meat.
Also: a piece of cheese, a slice of bread, a jar of coffee, a box of eggs.
More than one: two packets of rice, three tins of soup.
rules.mistake: Not: two packet of rice. Say: two packets of rice.

rules.title: Instructions: first, then, after that, finally
rule: An instruction starts with the verb: Cut the onions. Add the rice.
No I or you, and no s: Mix it. Not: You mixes it.
No: Don't + verb: Don't boil the soup.
Put the steps in order: First, … Then … After that, … Finally, …
Finally is only for the last step.
rules.mistake: Not: You cut the onions. Say: Cut the onions.

practice.why: Then is for a step in the middle.

practice.why: An instruction starts with the verb, with no s.

After that, ___ the rice and the tomatoes with a spoon.
practice.why: An instruction: the verb, with no s.

practice.q: ___ , boil the water. Then add the rice. Finally, add salt.
practice.why: The first step starts with first.

yourTurn.prompt: How do you make a cup of tea, or a drink you like? Write four steps. Use first, then, after that and finally.
yourTurn.model: First, boil some water. Then put a tea bag in a cup. After that, add the hot water and wait three minutes. Finally, add a little milk and mix it with a spoon.

text.title: The back of a packet of rice
text.body:
PRACTICE LABEL: this product is not real.

GOLDEN FIELD RICE · 1 kg

HOW TO COOK
Boil 2 cups of water in a pan.
Add 1 cup of rice and a little salt.
Cook for 12 minutes.
Keep in a cupboard.
Best before: 03/2027

RECIPE: EASY VEGETABLE RICE
For 2 people
You need:
1 cup of rice
1 onion
2 carrots
1 tin of tomatoes
2 spoons of oil
salt and pepper

What to do:
1. First, cut the onion and the carrots into small pieces.
2. Then heat the oil in a big pan. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
3. After that, add the carrots, the tomatoes and the rice. Mix with a spoon.
4. Then add 2 cups of water. Boil for 12 minutes.
5. Finally, add salt and pepper, and put it on the plates.

model.title: A recipe: cheese on toast
model.body:
Cheese on toast · for 1 person
You need:
2 slices of bread
a piece of cheese, about 50 grams
a little butter
pepper
What to do:
First, put the bread in the oven for 2 minutes.
Then put a little butter on the bread.
After that, cut the cheese into slices and put it on the bread.
Put it in the oven again for 5 minutes.
Finally, add a little pepper and put it on a plate.

model.title: Jollof rice
lines: Jollof rice is my favourite dish. It's from Ghana.
First, cut two onions and cook them in oil.
Then add two tins of tomatoes and a little pepper. Cook it for ten minutes.
After that, add the rice and some water. Mix it with a spoon.
How long do you cook it?
About twenty-five minutes. Finally, add salt and put it on the plates.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the stall conversation in pairs. Then change the food and the amounts: a packet of, a tin of, a jar of, a piece of.
Day 2: recipe chain. One learner says a step with first, the next says a step with then, and so on to finally.
Day 3: the task. Each learner explains a dish from home in four or five steps. Then you are the stallholder, and they buy what they need.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their recipes aloud. Can the class follow them?
